boundaries: badComponentSourceReason's refusal list (3212-3221: symbolId, lfsGroup, montageId, nativeVideo, isNullLayer, isEffectLayer, isGuideLayer, isWidgetLayer — 8 checks) is MISSING `isEffectorLayer`, even though getEffectiveStrokes' own equivalent early-return (app.js:2973, C21k, cited by line only: `if(ld.isNullLayer||ld.isEffectLayer||ld.isGuideLayer||ld.isWidgetLayer||ld.isEffectorLayer)return[];`) treats `isEffectorLayer` IDENTICALLY to the four sibling flags that ARE refused here — all five mean 'no real strokes to speak of'. Confirmed NOT a redundant case (unlike a folder layer, which timeline.js:1011 always sets `isNullLayer=true` alongside `isFolderLayer=true`, so folder layers are already caught via isNullLayer): timeline.js:2452 sets `isEffectorLayer=true` standalone, with no accompanying isNullLayer. An effector layer converted via convertLayerToComponent/convertLayersToComponent would silently pass the guard and get its (contentless) `.frames` cloned into a symLayer — the exact 'silently drop what it actually stands for' failure mode this function's own header comment (3203-3211) was written to prevent for the eight refused kinds. Not fixed here (census scope only); flagged for the next behavioral pass.

Every LIVE write into `state.symbols`: convertLayerToComponent (3295, `state.symbols[symId]={name,totalFrames,fps,layers:[symLayer]}`), convertLayersToComponent (3428, `state.symbols[symId]={name:'Composant',totalFrames,fps,layers:symLayers}`), importForeignSymbolTree (3511, `state.symbols[newId]={name,totalFrames,fps,layers:clonedLayers}`, one call per foreign symbol node in the tree, recursive), createComponentFromForeignProject (3527, `state.symbols[symId]={name,totalFrames,fps,layers:clonedLayers}` for the foreign project's OWN root). exposeSymbolProperty mutates an EXISTING entry only (`sym.exposedProps.push(entry)`, 3262) and never creates one.

Every LIVE write into `state.layers`/`userLayers` (the INSTANCE side): convertLayerToComponent mutates `ld` IN PLACE (no splice) — `ld.symbolId=symId;ld.locked=true;ld.symPlayMode='once';ld.symSpeed=1;ld.symPlacedAt=0;ld.symSingleFrame=0` (3302), then `ld.frames=[]` followed by a fresh all-empty/keyframe-0 array (3313); `delete ld.rig` (3294) beforehand. convertLayersToComponent removes every selected source (`state.layers.splice(indices[k],1);userLayers.splice(indices[k],1)`, descending k, 3432) THEN inserts one brand-new `newLd`/`newUl` at `insertAt=indices[0]` (3463-3464): `newLd={name:'Composant',symbolId:symId,locked:true,visible:true,symPlayMode:'once',symSpeed:1,symPlacedAt:0,symSingleFrame:0,frames:[],groups:...}` (3433-3434), then the firstSrc field-lift block (3442-3460, see below). placeComponentInstance creates a fresh layer via `createUserLayer(layerName)` (app.js:377, out of scope, cited by name only) and stamps the SAME six instance fields (`symbolId,locked,symPlayMode,symSpeed,symPlacedAt,symSingleFrame`, 3539) with no `symMatrix` (left unset = identity placement, per its own lead-in comment 3530-3531) and no rig/frames work (createUserLayer's own frames are already correctly-sized and empty).

NO componentFrame stamp is ever written by any of the three instance-creating paths (convertLayerToComponent 3302, convertLayersToComponent 3433, placeComponentInstance 3539) — each one's own comment (3303-3312 is the fullest) explains why: resolveSymbolFrameIdx (app.js:3557+ vicinity, cited by name only) checks an explicit componentFrame BEFORE symPlayMode, so stamping frame 0 on a freshly-created instance would pin it there for the whole timeline and defeat the just-set `symPlayMode:'once'` — a previously-shipped bug (2026-07-28) this scope's own comment documents as already fixed.

The guard-order fix at 3328-3339 (convertLayersToComponent): documents that the pre-filter at 3327 (`indices=...filter(function(i){return !!state.layers[i];})`) USED TO also silently drop already-`symbolId` layers as part of the SAME filter, BEFORE the type-guard loop (3340-3343, calling badComponentSourceReason per index) ever ran — so badComponentSourceReason's own 'un composant' refusal toast was unreachable for that specific case, and a selection of [instance, plain layer] silently produced a one-layer component with the instance discarded and no toast (measured live per the comment, 2 selected → 1 inside, no toast). Fixed by narrowing the filter to existence-only (3327) and running the full type-guard loop (3340-3343) AFTER it, over the still-symbolId-inclusive set.

The COMPLETE per-symLayer field-transfer field list in the 3402-3470 tail (the IIFE at 3414-3427, run once per symLayer `sl`/source `src` pair, k=index): deep-cloned when `src[f]!=null&&sl[f]==null&&!skip(f)` (3424) — effects, pathFx, blendKeys, parentKeys, parentsMore, expressions, exprControls, timeLink, markers, followPath, textAnimators, shapeNames (12 fields); primitive-copied under the same guard (3425) — layerUid, parentLayerUid, parentLayerUidB, matteSourceLayerUid, inPoint, outPoint, threeD, motionBlur, shy, keyLock, channel, isTextLayer, color, effectsFrom (14 fields). `skip(f)` (3423) is true only for symLayer k===0 (the topmost/first selected source) AND only for the 10 fields in `lifted` (3420: duplicator, exprControls, expressions, inPoint, outPoint, motionBlur, parentLayerUid, parentLayerUidB, threeD, timeLink) — of these, 9 actually intersect one of the two field lists above (duplicator intersects neither list, so its own `lifted` membership is a no-op inside the IIFE; it is dropped from every inner symLayer regardless of k, consistent with duplicator being outer-instance-only). For symLayer k>=1 (non-topmost sources), these same 9 fields ARE copied onto that source's OWN inner symLayer if present — i.e. only the TOPMOST selected source's matching fields get promoted to the outer instance; every other selected source's own copies of the same fields land on ITS OWN symLayer instead, neither lost nor double-applied.

Fields set on every symLayer OUTSIDE the IIFE, in the `.map()` builder itself (3357-3400), unconditionally: name, visible, locked(=false), frames (deep clone), motion/motionStatic/elementMotion (deep clone if present), groups (remapped clone, see below), rig (via cloneRigForSymbol, then deleted from src), matteMode, blendMode, mattesMore (uid/mode pairs only, per-entry).

`lipSync` (a real per-layer field — set by lipsync.js:46-48, read back by timeline.js:2540 and included in exportJSON's own complete per-layer field list, timeline.js:2117) is ABSENT from BOTH forEach field lists (3424/3425) and from the `.map()` builder (3357-3400) — silently dropped by convertLayersToComponent for every selected source, unlike the sibling layer-split helper (timeline.js:1235's own field list, which explicitly includes 'lipSync' alongside 'blendKeys'/'expressions'/etc.). Not fixed here; the complete per-layer field-list comparison this scope's own lead-in comment (3402-3413) already performed against exportJSON evidently did not include this field. convertLayerToComponent has no equivalent gap for `lipSync` (or any other ld-level field) since the original `ld` object is reused in place as the outer instance — its own `.lipSync` (if any) simply stays on it untouched; only frames/groups/rig are physically relocated into the new symLayer (3284-3294).

"Topmost source wins" precedence, the newLd (outer instance) field-lift block (3442-3460), all reading `firstSrc=state.layers[indices[0]]` captured at 3431 BEFORE the splice-out loop (3432) removes it from state.layers: inPoint/outPoint (3442-3443, `!=null` guard), timeLink (3444, deep clone), parentLayerUid/parentLayerUidB (3445-3446), expressions (3447, deep clone), exprControls (3452, deep clone, guarded additionally on `.length`), threeD/motionBlur (3458-3459, boolean-coerced via truthy-guard-then-`=true`, never explicitly reset to false/omitted), duplicator (3460, deep clone). Exactly the 10 fields named in `lifted` (3420) land here and ONLY here for symLayer k=0's own matching values — every other selected source's copy of the same 10 fields (if any) is preserved on ITS OWN inner symLayer per the previous finding, not discarded and not promoted.

`exposeSymbolProperty`'s written entry shape (3261): `{key,label,targetStrokeId,targetField,default}` — `key` is minted here (`'ep_'+Date.now().toString(36)+'_'+Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,6)`, 3260), not caller-supplied. Pushed onto `sym.exposedProps` (3259/3262, lazily initialized array). Readers: getEffectiveStrokes' own exposedProps block (app.js:3152-3167, C21k, cited by line only) — the SOLE evaluator of `targetField`, resolving `SMMotion.valueAtFrame(ld,ep.key,frameIdx)` per instance per frame, treating the `'__visible'` sentinel as 'drop this stroke from the output entirely when val<50' (never writing it onto the stroke dict) and every OTHER targetField as a real serialized-stroke-dict field to overwrite (opacity divided by 100 and clamped to [0,1]; anything else written verbatim) — and motion.js's propsFor (:179-182), which lists every `ep.key` as an ordinary keyable Motion property on any holder whose `.symbolId` resolves to this symbol, re-registering display metadata (label/default) via registerExposedPropMeta every call rather than once at exposure time (matching this function's own idempotent-registration call at 3263).

`instantiateForeignProjectAsComponent` and `createComponentFromForeignProject`/`importForeignSymbolTree` have NO try/catch anywhere in this scope, and NEITHER `pushUndoLayers` (tweens.js:4896, cited by name only) NOR its own snapshot builder `layersSnapshotNow` (tweens.js:4845, cited by line only, confirmed by direct read) ever serializes `state.symbols` — only `state.layers`, `cameraKeys`, `imageMeshes`, folder/link-group metadata, `motionArcs`, `tweenEasing`, `tweenOverrides` are captured, and `restoreLayersSnapshot` (tweens.js:4915, cited by line only) never touches `state.symbols` either. Consequence, confirmed by reading both functions directly rather than assumed: `pushUndo(true)` at 3550 (called BEFORE any state.symbols mutation) means an undo AFTER instantiateForeignProjectAsComponent restores `state.layers` (removing the newly-placed instance layer) but leaves EVERY `state.symbols` entry this call tree created — the top-level component from createComponentFromForeignProject (3527) plus one entry per nested foreign component recursively deep-copied by importForeignSymbolTree (3511) — as permanent orphans, unreferenced by any instance and never cleaned up. The identical orphan risk applies to convertLayerToComponent/convertLayersToComponent's own state.symbols writes (3295/3428) for the same reason (no state.symbols coverage in the undo snapshot at all), not specific to the foreign-import path or to a thrown exception — 'partial failure' and 'ordinary undo after success' land in the exact same orphaned-symbol state, since nothing here ever removes a `state.symbols[id]` entry once created.

`importForeignSymbolTree`'s idMap remaps ONLY symbol ids (`foreignSymId -> newId`, stamped at 3508 before recursing, to guard the shouldn't-happen cyclic case) — every `l.symbolId` inside a cloned layer is rewritten through it (3510/3526), but `layerUid`, `parentLayerUid`/`parentLayerUidB`, every `strokeId` inside `l.frames[*].strokes[*]`, `groups` keys, and `matteSourceLayerUid` are copied VERBATIM from the foreign project's JSON (plain `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`, 3509/3525) with no remap at all. The comment at 3498-3502 only claims the SYMBOL-id collision is impossible ('both projects mint ids from the same genSymbolId() scheme') — genSymbolId (3202) mints from `Date.now()+Math.random()`, and layerUid/strokeId are minted by other, unexamined generators (out of scope) that are not shown to share this same collision-avoidance property; a raw id collision on any of the un-remapped fields between the importing project and the foreign one is not ruled out by anything in this scope.

`_symbolPaperLayers` (module var, declared app.js:3192, C21k) is read-then-lazily-populated by ONE function in this scope, ensureSymbolPaperLayers (3195 read/early-return, 3196-3200 populate, 3201 write back to `_symbolPaperLayers[symId]`) — its own body creates one real `new Layer(...)` per symbol sub-layer (3198, `insertBelow(arcLayer)`, initially `.visible=false`), inserted into the live Paper.js document immediately (not a throwaway/uninserted query object, unlike C21i's own `boneCache` temp paths). No other function in this scope reads or writes `_symbolPaperLayers`; its own sole external caller is enterSymbol (app.js:4182, cited by line only, later slice), which flips the returned layers' visibility/opacity on when entering the symbol.

Call order inside every one of the three top-level entry points (convertLayerToComponent 3276/3314, convertLayersToComponent 3345/3468, instantiateForeignProjectAsComponent 3550/3554) is IDENTICAL and appears exactly once per function, at the very start and very end: `saveAllLayerFrames();pushUndo(true);` first (before any state.symbols/state.layers mutation — `pushUndo(true)`'s own `true` argument is `pushUndoLayers`'s `alreadySaved` parameter, tweens.js:4896, cited by line only, skipping its own internal saveAllLayerFrames call since the caller already made one explicitly, avoiding a double save), then `loadFrame(state.currentFrame);renderOS();renderArcs();updateUI();if(window.renderSymbolTabs)renderSymbolTabs();` last, immediately before the function's own showToast call. NONE of the three calls `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` or `renderTimeline()` directly in this scope — both are presumed reached indirectly through `updateUI()` (timeline.js, cited by name only), not reproduced here. `SMStoryboard.addInstanceAuto(symId)` (cited by name only) is called once per entry point, keyed by `symId` alone (not by instance), at a point where the NEW component exists in `state.symbols` but the corresponding INSTANCE may not yet exist in `state.layers`/have its `symbolId` stamped yet: convertLayerToComponent calls it at 3296, one line after the state.symbols write (3295) and BEFORE `ld.symbolId=symId` is set (3302); convertLayersToComponent calls it at 3429, right after the state.symbols write (3428) and BEFORE the source splice-out (3432)/newLd creation (3463); instantiateForeignProjectAsComponent calls it at 3552, after createComponentFromForeignProject (3551) returns symId and BEFORE placeComponentInstance (3553) creates the instance layer.

A future pass should add it to either the deep-clone loop (3424) or a dedicated line, matching the sibling helper's own treatment — not changed here.

Neither `layersSnapshotNow` (tweens.js:4845) nor `restoreLayersSnapshot` (tweens.js:4915) ever reads or writes `state.symbols` — every state.symbols-creating construct in this scope (convertLayerToComponent, convertLayersToComponent, createComponentFromForeignProject/importForeignSymbolTree) leaves a permanent orphan entry behind after any undo of the action that created it, with no code path anywhere that removes a state.symbols[id] entry once minted. This is the same class of bug CLAUDE.md §1 names for 'a live reference never survives save/reload' — except here it survives TOO WELL (an entry nothing references any more is never garbage-collected, growing the exported project file's `symbols` object indefinitely across repeated convert/undo cycles). Not changed here; flagged as a real memory/file-size leak worth its own behavioral pass, not just a census note.

importForeignSymbolTree/createComponentFromForeignProject remap only `symbolId` through `idMap`; every other id-bearing field (layerUid, parentLayerUid(B), matteSourceLayerUid, per-stroke strokeId, group keys) is copied verbatim from the foreign project's JSON. The design comment's own collision-avoidance claim (3498-3502) covers only the symbolId case; a future audit should confirm whether layerUid/strokeId collisions between two independently-authored projects are actually impossible (e.g. if their minting scheme also derives from Date.now()+random) or whether importing two projects with overlapping ids could silently merge unrelated parent-links/mattes/groups once inside the SAME state.layers array (a nested component's own OWN layers stay isolated inside state.symbols, but the outer instance layerUid created by createComponentFromForeignProject/placeComponentInstance is fresh via createUserLayer — the risk is confined to ids INSIDE the deep-copied symbol trees, never surfaced into the importing project's own top-level state.layers). Not verified further here.

convertLayerToComponent never transfers `effects`/`pathFx`/`blendKeys`/`expressions`/`markers`/etc. into the new symLayer (only frames/groups/rig move) — by design, since `ld` itself stays the instance and keeps those fields (CLAUDE.md §8). Whether any of those ld-level fields (particularly `pathFx`, a per-shape path effect) are still meaningfully applied to the FLATTENED inner content once getEffectiveStrokes' symbolId branch (C21k) takes over rendering was not traced in this census (would require reading pathFx's own render-time consumer, out of scope) — flagged as worth checking in a future pass, not claimed as a confirmed bug.
